title: Payment solutions for UAE businesses: A guide
summary: Discover what types of payment solutions are most popular for UAE businesses, how to choose the right one for you, and compare leading payment providers.
body_markdown:
Getting paid in the UAE used to be quite straightforward: a customer either handed over cash or simply paid by card. But today, businesses can take payments through websites, payment links, QR codes, smartphones, social media, and more.


That’s where different payment solutions come in. By offering one or several payment solutions, you can give your customers more flexibility when they pay.


But the right setup can look very different from one business to another. You might want to:


- Accept payments directly through social media DMs


- Offer popular payment methods such as Apple Pay and Google Pay


- Sell across several payment channels at once


- Keep costs predictable with transparent pricing and no subscription fees


With plenty of payment solutions available in the UAE, the challenge is figuring out which type – and which provider – fits the way you sell.


In this guide, we’ll cover:


- What types of payment solutions are there?


- How to choose a payment solution for your business


- 6 popular payment solution providers in the UAE

### What types of payment solutions are there?


Payment solution What is it, and when could you use it?


Tap to Pay


Tap to Pay turns an NFC-enabled phone into a payment terminal. It's ideal for businesses accepting payments across multiple locations. With Ziina, you can also let staff members accept payments directly on their phones.


Payment links


Payment links are URLs you can share via social media, email, or SMS. Customers simply click the link to open a ready-made checkout page, enter their payment details, and pay.


QR codes


Customers scan a QR code with their phone camera to open a payment page and enter their details. You can display QR codes almost anywhere, from restaurant tables and shop counters to pop-up events.


Payment gateways (online checkout)


A payment gateway lets customers pay through your website or app. You can integrate one with Shopify or WooCommerce using a plugin, or use an API to add a hosted checkout page or embedded payment form to a custom website.


POS machines


Point-of-sale (POS) terminals let customers pay in person by tapping or inserting their cards. They're useful for physical stores, but you'll need to buy or rent the devices, keep them charged, and maintain them.


## How to choose the right payment solution for your business


Let’s be clear: you don’t need five different tools to start accepting payments. Some UAE businesses will set up one method and stick with it for years, while others will want to add new payment methods as they grow.


To figure out which solution fits your needs, ask:


- Where do your customers pay most often?


For instance, if most of your transactions come through social media, then you’d likely be better off choosing payment links over traditional invoices.


- How automated do you need sales to be?


Or, in other words: how involved do you want to be in the checkout process? For example, payment links can feel more personal, but you might need to send them to customers manually, which can quickly become tedious if you get tens or hundreds of messages a day. On the other hand, if you add a payment gateway to your website, customers can check out without you having to step in each time.


Once you’ve figured out which payment solution you want to use, you’ll need to look for a provider… a process which comes with its own set of questions:


- Which payment methods do your customers expect?


In the UAE, that usually means debit and credit cards, plus


[Apple Pay](https://ziina.com/card/apple-pay) and


[Google Pay](https://ziina.com/card/google-pay) . Different providers will offer a different set of payment acceptance methods.


- What are the costs of using each solution?


To get the most accurate idea of costs, we’d recommend looking past transaction fees and at the total cost. For example, some providers might charge monthly subscription fees, varying currency conversion fees, or have minimum balance requirements.


- What are the onboarding and payout timelines?


If you want to start accepting payments as quickly as possible, it’s important that the onboarding and verification process is quick and simple. Plus, quick cashouts will make it easier to manage your cash flow more effectively.


- Are you planning on scaling your business?


If you want to move from offline sales to a payment gateway, for instance, all-in-one providers let you offer several solutions without the extra hassle of stitching together multiple gateways and apps: instead, if you sell through a new channel, your payments will be processed by your current provider and your funds will land right in your existing payment account.
